ambiguities_or_notes: Every source block (28) has a matching target block, with page markers, numbering, quotation structure, and italics preserved.

Website Circle of Reading paragraphs served as the first draft; each was re-read against the Russian and revised where it drifted (omissions, additions, generic he/his, terminology, attribution form); blocks 2, 3 had no website counterpart and were translated fresh.

The opening thought (two paragraphs), which had no website draft, is translated fresh. In Tolstoy's comment on Luke 14:26 the source prints «в стихе 24-м 8-й гл. Луки» (v stikhe 24-m 8-y gl. Luki, 'in verse 24 of chapter 8 of Luke'); the words meant are Luke 8:21 (quoted earlier this day as Luke 8:20–21), so the English reads 'verse 21'. «Соблазняют» (soblaznyayut, 'tempt') is rendered 'are a temptation to', keeping «соблазн» = 'temptation', and «личность» (lichnost') is 'personality'.

Source observation: [22] The text cites «стихе 24-м 8-й гл. Луки» (Luke 8:24), but the words referred to ('my mother and my brothers are those who hear the word of God and do it') are Luke 8:21 (Luke 8:24 is the storm on the lake); corrected to 'verse 21' in the English.
